note: Long unsupported stretch in extreme heat is a real hazard, but riders are actively compensating with extra water and an early start.
Unchecked anchors and a novice leader are real gaps, though it's top-rope rather than lead climbing.
Fast current, a steep bank, and an unrailed overlook near young kids who won't be watched every second are real hazards, though life vests are planned this time.
The route looks extreme but every real hazard is thoroughly mitigated by a certified guide and redundant, tested systems.
Starting an exposed above-treeline hike right as afternoon storms are forecast risks lightning exposure with no rain gear.
Improper food storage in an area with recent bear activity is a real gap, though no direct encounter occurred.
A narrow trail with a steep drop, run solo with deteriorating weather and no gear, verges on severe but the storm isn't certain yet.
Strong crosswinds on a narrow, unguarded viaduct could push a rider into traffic, bordering on severe.
The only real hazard (possible afternoon wind) is proactively managed with PFDs and an early turnaround.
Backcountry travel without a beacon is a real gap, but staying on gentle slopes below treeline limits the danger.
Crossing an untested snow bridge is risky, though the group did go across one at a time.
Getting cut off by the rising tide on the walkway is a real possibility if they misjudge timing.
Ill-fitting borrowed life jackets and an afternoon-wind crossing on open water are real but partially mitigated gaps.
No guardrail on loose gravel switchbacks is a real hazard, though proper footwear is explicitly advised.
Routine supervised swim in a bounded, calm area, though the supervision is a friend watching rather than a trained lifeguard.
A previous ankle tweak and a dead zone past the second bridge add some risk, but the runner shared the route and timing beforehand.
Several precautions (beacon, radio) are missing for a terrain-trap gully, though it's inbounds and patrolled on request.
Wet rock is a real hazard for the climb, but mitigated with extra chalk and checking holds beforehand; could be read as negligible (0) given the modest 12m height.
The raccoon-into-coolers hazard is minor but real and is explicitly and fully mitigated with a bear box and sealed food; borders on negligible risk (0).
A genuine no-shoulder road hazard, but brief and actively managed with single file riding and lights; borders on elevated risk (2) given proximity to traffic.
Tide tables weren't checked and the rocks turn slick as the tide comes in - a real, unaddressed hazard, but nothing indicates conditions are already severe.
